en: Itivuttaka 61:

Tikanipāta, Dutiyavagga (The Second Chapter) Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having thus spoken, the Well-Farer, the Teacher, further said this: "Those who have not abandoned the three things—lust, hatred, and delusion—will not cross over the realm of death, even though they may go for a hundred years. But those who have abandoned the three things—lust, hatred, and delusion—cross over the realm of death, even if they go for only a single day."
The Discourse on the Eye.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:
"Bhikkhus, there are these three eyes."
Which three?
The fleshly eye, the divine eye, and the wisdom-eye—
these, monks, are the three eyes.”
The Blessed One spoke this matter.
Regarding this, it is said:
“The fleshly eye and the divine eye,”
And the unsurpassed eye of wisdom—
these three eyes the Supreme Person has proclaimed.
The arising of the fleshly eye,
the path to the divine eye—
whence knowledge arose.
The unsurpassed eye of wisdom;
by the acquisition of which eye one is liberated from all suffering.”
This matter too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The second [sutta].
